links.outcome: Reading level of LLM-generated ROP patient materials versus recommended 6th-grade level
links.effect: TOA brochure above 6th-grade level; LLM materials also above recommended level. Ateşman: GPT-4.0 and Gemini ~9th-10th grade, GPT-4o mini 11th-12th grade.
links.quote: The reading levels of these materials were determined to be above the recommended level, not aligned with the norms stated in the literature.

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education materials
links.effect: LLM outputs remained above the 6th-grade level; simplification prompts (P1/P2) significantly improved Bezirci-Yılmaz readability only for GPT-4.0 (p=0.005, p=0.012), not GPT-4o mini or Gemini.
links.quote: When comparing the initial responses of the LLMs (GPT-4.0, Gemini, and GPT-4o mini) with their responses in the P1 and P2 formats, a statistically significant increase in readability was observed only in the responses of GPT-4.0 (p=0.005 and p=0.012, respectively).

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and comprehensiveness of LLM patient materials against TOA guidelines
links.effect: GPT-4.0 accuracy significantly higher than Gemini (p=0.001); GPT-4.0 more comprehensive than GPT-4o mini (p=0.045) and Gemini (p=0.001). GPT-4.0 screening criteria answer mismatched TOA standards.
links.quote: When comparing the accuracy scores of the initial responses from the LLMs, GPT-4.0’s accuracy scores were found to be statistically significantly higher than those of Gemini (p=0.001).

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM clinical content with local (Turkish) screening guidelines
links.effect: GPT-4.0 gave screening criteria (<30 weeks or <1,500 g) matching UK, not TOA criteria (<34 weeks or <1,700 g), risking misinformation.
links.quote: GPT-4.0’s response for this question (“infants born before 30 weeks or weighing less than 1,500 grams”) was comparable to the screening criteria employed in the United Kingdom but not with the TOA standards for Türkiye.
